cs3.statement: For every simple 3-tree H, every subgraph G of H, every A subset V(G), every integer r>=1, each source-standard LCA guard S in a width-3 decomposition of G, and each assigned subset X_S of V(G), the number of truncated distance vectors (cap_r(d_G(x,s)))_{s in S} for x in X_S is at most C(r+2)^3 for one absolute C.
cs3.main_conjecture_to_cs3: A CS3 vector is a profile on S, where |S|<=8. The conjectured bound gives at most 8*C3*r^3 non-all-infinity vectors plus at most one all-infinity vector.
cs3.cs3_to_main_conjecture: The source LCA family has at most 4|A| guards of size at most 8. For a vertex assigned to a valid guard, the profile on A is determined by its G-distance vector to that guard. Summing gives O(r^3|A|).
cs3.guard_scope_correction: The primary-source LCA lemma builds bags from a tree decomposition of the measured graph G. For G subgraph H, intersecting H's bags with V(G) gives a valid width-3 decomposition; guards are actual vertices of G and distances are measured in G. The source itself does not assign unique X_S regions; any fixed valid-guard assignment suffices.

claims.claim: A valid guard-distance signature determines the truncated landmark profile in the same graph.
Vertices can have different signatures to a standard LCA guard and identical profiles to the original landmark set.
claims.example: G is the tree with edges ac,cx,cy; A={a,c}; decomposition bags {c,y} root and {a,c,x} child; the latter is a source-standard guard. At r>=2, x,y have A-profile (2,1) but guard signatures (2,1,0) and (2,1,2). G is a subgraph of simple 3-tree K4.

claims.claim: An Omega(r^4) guard-signature family can coexist with the main conjecture.
claims.reason: For S subset V(G), signatures are profiles on at most eight landmarks, so Omega(r^4) signatures would itself contradict the conjectured O(r^3 k) bound at k<=8.

claims.claim: Joret-Rambaud's treewidth-3 lower construction is an eligible simple-treewidth-3 counterexample.
claims.reason: The t=3 construction contains a K3,3 minor, whereas simple 3-trees and their subgraphs are planar.

claims.claim: The main simple-treewidth-3 profile conjecture is true or false.

prior_art.beaudou_et_al: Explicitly conjecture O_t(r^t k) for simple treewidth at most t; prove O_t(r^(t+1)k) for treewidth t and provide at most 4|A| LCA guards of size at most 2(t+1).
prior_art.joret_rambaud: Give an Omega_t(r^(t+1)) treewidth-t lower construction for constant landmarks, an Omega(r^3) planar lower bound, and an O(r^4) planar upper bound.
prior_art.novelty_verdict: The equivalence and finite example are elementary scope clarification, not a publication-level structural result.

proved: Main conjecture implies CS3 uniformly for every guard and every assigned subset.
CS3 plus the source LCA guard family implies the main conjecture.
The four-vertex overcount example is a valid simple-treewidth-3 subgraph and uses a standard guard bag.
open: Prove O(r^3 k) for all partial simple 3-trees, or find a valid asymptotic counterexample.
Find a corridor-specific counting principle genuinely weaker than arbitrary constant-size landmark profile complexity.
failed: Treating CS3 as an independent easier intermediate lemma: it is equivalent to the full conjecture up to constants.
